newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan king, PLO's Arafat to discuss Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Jordan king, PLO's Arafat to discuss Mideast.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will meet on Monday to discuss the deepening crisis in the Middle East peace process after the latest suicide attacks, officials said.

They said Arafat would visit Amman to seek King Hussein's support in the face of Israeli pressure on him after last Wednesday's bombings in a Jerusalem market, which the Palestinian leader says are being exploited by Israel to backtrack on peace commitments.

Jordan has warned Israel that tough security measures against the Palestinians in the fight against Moslem militants following the bombings that killed 13 people would only backfire and bring more violence.
The king has said the bloodshed could have been precipitated by growing frustrations with a stalled peace process and anger over an accelerated Jewish settlement drive in the West Bank.
On Sunday he again expressed during an audience with a delegation of visiting Israeli parliamentarians his deep concern over the fate of the peace process.
"We have to move quickly and with determination to rectify the peace path before it is too late," he told the delegation of Knesset (parliament) members headed by Israeli-Arab member Salah Tarif.

In a snub to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Natanyahu, who accuses Arafat of not doing enough to crack down on Palestinian militants, the king gave a ringing vote of confidence to the Palestinian leader, saying he was doing his utmost to combat militants.

Jordan is worried by the repercussions of renewed violence in Palestinian territories on its own stability. The kingdom's 4.2 million people have close ethnic ties with Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
King Hussein has expressed increasing exasperation with Netanyahu's policies, publicly doubting his resolve to advance the peace process.
Jordan supports the Palestinian view that Israel has been stalling on implementing a 1993 interim peace accord.
